postings.title: (Senior) Design Engineer (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As a (Senior) Design Engineer within the system integration team, you will find yourself at the heart of product development related efforts across Isar Aerospace. You will be responsible for fluids related hardware design and development, from its early conception, to its qualification and integration into the final product. Additionally, you will oversee integration of various systems and components into the global launch vehicle, while ensuring their functionality. Furthermore, you will work closely with a passionate team, as well as the rest of highly motivated colleagues across other teams/departments. You will play a crucial role in getting our orbital launch vehicle designed and built.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Fluid hardware focused design and development: High pressure & cryogenic pipes, manifolds, fluid fittings, fluid storages, and their support structures

- Fluid hardware qualification: Test plan definition and documentation / test execution oversight

- Implementation and maintenance of engineering change requests.

- Integration of designs into global assemblies

- Product requirement & verification definition efforts

- Preparation of detailed product development road maps and maintenance of their timelines

- Preparation of design reviews, risk assessments, trade-off studies, etc.

- Communication with the affected stakeholders (e.g. production, assembly, other engineering departments) to ensure efficient development of products

- Interface management

Qualification Checklist

- Min. bachelor’s degree in aerospace engineering or similar

- 2+ years of experience in hardware design and development

- Proficiency with design engineering tools such as NX, TeamCenter, Solidworks or similar

- Experience with product lifecycle management (PLM) and product data management (PDM)

- Strong knowledge in various manufacturing methods (e.g. milling, turning, metal sheet, composite or additive manufacturing)

- Experience with standards (e.g. DIN, EN, ISO, AN/AS, LN)

- Strong understanding of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T)

- Results orientated with ability to plan and deliver against project deadlines

- Resilient, self-motivated and able to work well under pressure

- Highly organized and proactive with high attention to detail

- Fluent English language skills

Bonus Skills

- Experience in launch vehicle design, manufacturing, or assembly techniques for structure and fluid systems

- Experience in aerospace hydraulic system component design

- General knowledge of aerospace/aviation hardware design

- Knowledge of fabrication, integration processes, and quality control relative to tubes/piping and machined components

- Hands-on hardware production or assembly experience

- Proficient German

- Lean production knowledge

Benefits

- Employee Participation Program: Share in our success through our virtual company share program

- 30 days of vacation: Enjoy the days off to relax and recharge

- Company pension plan: Secure your future with our company pension plan, featuring a 20% employer contribution after the probation period

- Subsidised lunch: Stay energised with delicious, subsidised lunches every day

- Public transport ticket: Commute with ease using a fully financed Deutschlandticket

- Childcare allowance: Receive a childcare allowance for your non-school-age children

- And Much More! Discover additional perks and benefits when you join our team.

Who we are

We are Isar Aerospace and we are at the forefront of New Space building a modern space business to enable faster, better and cheaper access to space.

Our mission is to help democratise space and use it for good in order to improve life on Earth now and for the future generations.

postings.title: (Senior) GNC Engineer - Navigation, Flight Software (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As a GNC Engineer at Isar Aerospace SE, you develop the guidance, navigation, and control systems that enable Spectrum to operate safely, accurately, and efficiently throughout its mission. You design, verify, and validate flight algorithms that determine the vehicle’s position, velocity, and attitude while steering it along its optimal trajectory during all phases of flight. By combining flight dynamics, state estimation, control theory, and high-fidelity simulation, you ensure robust performance in the presence of uncertainties and disturbances. Your work is essential to maximizing mission success, payload capability, and the reliability of every Spectrum launch.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Architect the next generation navigation system for an orbital launch vehicle

- Perform Navigation algorithm tuning and improvements based on flight data

- Responsible for ground and flight integrity monitoring for safety critical navigation systems

- Ownership of all GNSS applications on the vehicle

- Perform GNSS Integrity studies

Qualification Checklist

- BSc/MSc/PhD in Mechanical, Aerospace, Electrical or Robotics Engineering, Physics, Mathematics or similar

- Proficient in inertial navigation algorithms and Kalman filter techniques

- 3+ years of experience with GNSS receiver configurations and testing (GNSS simulator test setups)

- Strong understanding of integrity monitoring and jamming and spoofing resilience

- Experience with performing GNSS integrity studies and analysis

- Experience in developing with MATLAB

- Experience in developing with Python and C++

- Proficient with Git

- Maintain and drive a high standard of technical documentation

- Fluent in English

Bonus Skills

- Experience with RTK and PPK

- Strong understanding of discrete signal processing techniques

postings.title: AIT Operations Engineer - Launch Vehicle (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As part of the Launch Vehicle AIT (Assembly, Integration, and Testing) team, you will be responsible for ensuring smooth, efficient, and timely integration activities. In addition, you will be participating in the change management process and work together with relevant stakeholders to drive up key performance indicators (KPIs) and follow-up on non-conformities.

Your Role in Our Space Mission

- Create, maintain, and optimize the launch vehicle AIT workflows

- Manage operational interfaces of the launcher integration team like the Testing, Logistics or Quality Assurance teams.

- Manage and improve the vehicle integration timeline.

- Create efficient tooling to plan, monitor, and optimize launcher integration activities.

- Participate in and drive engineering change management processes concerning launcher integration topics from initial change request through final hardware implementation on flight and nonflight systems.

- Serve as a key contributor to the non‑conformance process by assessing criticality, defining scope of impact, and developing/validating corrective and preventive actions.

- Act as AIT representative to internal stakeholders—including Design Engineering, Launch Operations, and Production—ensuring AIT requirements are understood and integrated into cross-functional decision-making.

- Identify, lead, and implement internal process improvements aimed at increasing efficiency, reducing rework, and strengthening data flow within AIT.

- Ensure safe execution of launcher integration activities by implementing PPE, ESD, and HSE rules together with the HSE team.

- Develop and realise concepts for AIT facilities across all Isar Aerospace sites.

Qualification Checklist

- BSc/MSc in Mechanical/Aerospace Engineering or similar

- Strong drive for continuous improvement and strong communication skills

- Experience in bottleneck analysis, line balancing methods, and OEE calculation

- Extensive experience in project management including setup, maintenance, and reporting of timelines, KPIs, and processes

- Experience in assembly and testing of complex systems (medical, aerospace, automotive or similar)

- Clean, organized, and structured way of work

- Basic knowledge in Python, C++, or similar

- Fluent in English

Bonus Skills

As AIT Technician, you will join us on the arctic island of Andøya, and – as part of a small local AIT team – support onsite assembly, integration, test, and launch activities. - Shaping the launch site: Continuously improve the AIT infrastructure, and help develop it to compete with world class AIT facilities around the globe

- High-Precision Assembly: Precise assembly of advanced space components

- Machining Carbon Fiber Composites: Working with cutting-edge carbon fibre materials

- Component and Assembly Testing: Validating the functionality of individual parts and complete assemblies

postings.title: Avionics Technician (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As an Avionics Technician within the AIT team, you will play a critical role in the final assembly, integration, and checkout of our launch vehicle's avionic and electromechanical systems. You will be responsible for routing and installing complex wire harnesses, integrating precision sensors and avionics units, and supporting critical test operations. This role requires a high degree of craftsmanship, working with both advanced composite and metallic structures, and operating safely around high-pressure and cryogenic fluid systems.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

Key Responsibilities

- Harness Routing & Installation: Route, secure, and install complex vehicle wire harnesses in accordance with engineering drawings and aerospace standards.

- Structural Bonding & Adhesives: Prepare surfaces and bond ClickBond clips and standoffs to metallic and composite structures. Apply aerospace-grade adhesives.

- Avionics Unit Installation: Install and mechanically secure telemetry modules, batteries, and other avionics enclosures.

- Precision Mechanical Assembly: Use torque wrenches and calibrated hand tools to mate structural and electrical components, ensuring strict adherence to torque specifications and engineering drawings.

- Crimping & Soldering: Perform high-reliability crimping, pinning, and soldering on flight connectors and wire splices.

- Rework & Modification: Execute precise rework and modifications on existing wire harnesses, connectors, and pinouts based on engineering change orders.

- Sensor Installation & Checkout: Install and connect critical flight sensors (pressure transducers, thermocouples, RTDs, accelerometers, etc.) and verify functionality.

- Fluid Connections: Install fluid lines using Swagelok fittings and components for instrumentation and purging systems.

- Hazardous Operations Support: Work in close proximity to or directly interface avionics components with Cryogenic Liquid Oxygen (LOX) and Liquid Propellant (LPP) systems, adhering to strict cleanliness (oxygen clean) and safety protocols.

- Electrical Checkouts: Utilize multimeters, megohmmeters, and specialized test equipment to perform continuity, isolation, and bonding checks.

- Testing & Troubleshooting: Conducting integrated system testing and pre-launch checkouts alone or alongside test engineers

Qualifications & Skills

- Completed vocational training as an aircraft mechanic, specializing in avionics technician, maintenance technician or comparable training in accordance with the requirements

- Proven experience as an avionics, electrical, or electromechanical technician in aerospace, aviation, or high-reliability manufacturing.

- Proficient with precision hand tools, calibrated torque wrenches, and electrical test equipment (multimeters).

- Experience working on both carbon fiber/composite and aluminum aerostructures.

- Strong knowledge of aerospace crimping, soldering, and harness manufacturing standards.

- Ability to read and interpret complex electrical schematics, wire lists, and mechanical engineering drawings.

- Ability to work in confined spaces and at heights.

- Familiarity with safety protocols surrounding high-pressure gases and cryogenics.

- High attention to detail and a strong commitment to flight safety and quality.

Qualification Checklist

- 2+ years of experience in aerospace, rocketry, aviation, or a high-reliability manufacturing environment (eg, defense, motorsports).

- Strong background in reading and interpreting complex engineering blueprints, electrical schematics, and wiring diagrams.

- Demonstrated experience with precision measuring tools, torque wrenches, crimp tools, and specialized aerospace hand tools.

- Comfortable working with hazardous materials, structural epoxies, primers, and solvents.

- Familiarity with the hazards of high-pressure systems, hazardous propellants, and cryogenic fluids (LOX/LPP).

- Fluent in English and German

- Ability to stand for long periods, crawl into tight spaces (inside rocket fairings or stages), and work from ladders or elevated platforms.

- Fine motor skills and dexterity for handling small components and delicate wiring.

- Ability to lift up to 35 lbs regularly.

Bonus Skills

- Certifications such as IPC/WHMA-A-620 (Requirements for Cable and Wire Harness Assemblies) or NASA-STD-8739.

- Prior experience with launch vehicle integration or test operations.

postings.title: Chief Quality  Inspector (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

The Chief Quality Inspector is the independent authority responsible for defining how product conformity is verified across manufacturing operations. This role establishes inspection strategies, verification methods, conformity assessment criteria, and competency standards to ensure objective evidence exists that every product meets defined requirements.

The position is driving a quality-at-source culture and a scalable inspection framework capable of supporting company growth. The Chief Quality Inspector ensures inspection activities provide reliable product acceptance decisions and robust evidence of compliance throughout the manufacturing lifecycle.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Define and govern the company inspection strategy, acceptance approaches, and verification methodologies.

- Establish conformity assessment criteria and ensure objective evidence supports all product acceptance decisions.

- Own inspection governance, standards, procedures, and inspection-related competency frameworks.

- Lead laboratory functions including material testing, metallography, composite testing, calibration activities, and failure investigations.

- Support process qualification activities by defining required verification and inspection evidence.

- Drive implementation of quality-at-source principles across manufacturing operations.

- Ensure inspection resources, technologies, and capabilities can scale with future production demand.

- Develop and maintain inspector training, qualification, certification, and recertification requirements.

- Partner with Manufacturing, Production Engineering, Product Assurance, and Supplier Quality to resolve conformity concerns and improve product quality.

- Provide clear conformity recommendations and inspection performance reporting to senior leadership.

Qualification Checklist

- Extensive experience in manufacturing quality, inspection, product assurance, or quality engineering leadership roles.

- Demonstrated expertise in inspection methods, conformity assessment, acceptance criteria, and verification planning.

- Strong understanding of incoming inspection, in-process inspection, final inspection, and release processes.

- Experience leading NDT disciplines including X-Ray, Computed Tomography (CT), Ultrasonic, and Dye Penetrant inspection.

- Knowledge of laboratory operations, materials testing, metallography, calibration systems, and failure analysis methods.

- Experience developing inspection standards, procedures, governance models, and competency frameworks.

- Ability to make objective conformity decisions based on technical evidence and risk assessment.

- Strong leadership capability with experience developing and managing multidisciplinary technical teams.

- Proven ability to implement scalable quality systems within fast-growing manufacturing organizations.

- Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and problem-solving skills.

- Strong analytical mindset with high attention to detail and commitment to product integrity.

- Professional proficiency in English; German language skills are advantageous.

Aim high, deliver relentlessly, act with integrity, and keep the mission first.

postings.title: Combustion Equipment Engineer (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

You will own the design, analysis, development and qualification of combustion equipment for liquid rocket engines, including gas generators and pre burners. As the technical responsible you translate engine level requirements into robust combustion device architectures and mature them through analysis, design, manufacturing and hot fire testing, ensuring safe, stable, testable and manufacturable solutions.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Own the design and development of liquid rocket engine combustion equipment, including gas generators, pre burners, their injector heads and combustion chambers, ignition systems and associated interfaces.

- Define component requirements, operating envelopes, interface conditions and technical budgets based on engine level performance, lifetime and operability needs.

- Perform preliminary and detailed sizing of combustion devices using first principles methods and appropriate analytical or numerical tools.

- Lead architecture and design trade offs covering injector concepts, mixture distribution, pressure drop, combustion efficiency, stability, ignition, cooling, materials and manufacturability.

- Plan, support and evaluate component and engine level test campaigns, including instrumentation definition, test predictions, data review and correlation of models with hot fire results.

- Investigate combustion anomalies and performance deviations, identify root causes and define technically justified corrective actions.

- Own the technical development roadmap for your hardware, including maturation activities, design reviews, manufacturing follow up and qualification planning.

- Work closely with the cycle, turbomachinery, valves, feed systems, controls, structures, thermal, manufacturing and test teams to deliver an integrated propulsion system.

Qualification Checklist

- MSc in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering or a comparable technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

- Several years in liquid rocket engine development, with significant responsibility for combustion device design, analysis, development or testing.

- Hands on experience with gas generators, pre burners or comparable high performance liquid propellant combustion devices.

- Excellent understanding of combustion, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, heat transfer and liquid rocket propulsion.

- Significant experience in injector or combustor sizing, particularly at very high or very low O/F, and in interpreting hot fire test data.

- Experience owning a development roadmap through design reviews and into qualification.

- Proficiency in Python, MATLAB or a comparable programming language.

- Strong technical ownership and the ability to make sound engineering decisions with incomplete early phase data.

- Fluent in English.

- Willingness to travel occasionally for test and launch operations.

Bonus Skills

- Experience with both gas generators and pre burners across different liquid rocket engine architectures.

- Experience with combustion stability, acoustic analysis, ignition transients or operability assessment.

- Experience with injector technologies such as coaxial, impinging, swirl or pintle concepts.

- Experience taking combustion hardware from initial sizing through manufacturing and hot fire qualification.

postings.title: Cybersecurity Engineer (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

You are a technical guardian of our digital environment. At Isar Aerospace, the systems, data and people that build our rockets are mission critical and protecting them takes someone who builds controls and then proves they hold.

We are looking for a hands-on Security Engineer who bridges the gap between Security Architecture and Operations. You are not just a consultant; you are a builder and an auditor. You wear two hats: the Engineer who designs and implements security controls, and the Technical Auditor who verifies that systems and operations meet the high standards required for a space company. You will act as the technical conscience of our environment, working across domains such as endpoints, identity, cloud, networks and applications.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Engineer security controls: design, implement and maintain security controls across our technology stack, defining the exact configurations and policies required to protect our systems, applications and data.

- Act as the technical auditor: you don’t just trust; you verify. Check the configurations of IT and engineering teams against security baselines and provide guidance to close gaps.

- Protect identity and access: help safeguard the keys to the kingdom through strong authentication, least privilege and privileged access controls across the environment.

- Detect and respond: use security monitoring and telemetry to separate signal from noise. When an alert fires, investigate the root cause and coordinate remediation.

- Define the hardening standard: develop and maintain secure configuration baselines and engineering standards for the systems in your scope. You define what “secure” looks like.

- Automate the defence: use scripting to automate security checks, streamline incident response and integrate disparate security tools.

- Collaborate and document: produce clear technical documentation and translate complex security requirements into runbooks that IT and engineering teams can execute.

Qualification Checklist

- Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security or a related field, or the equivalent through relevant certifications and hands-on experience.

- Experience: 3–5+ years in Information Security or Security Engineering, with hands-on ownership of security controls in a production environment.

- Hands-on Engineering: deep experience implementing security controls in at least one domain such as endpoint, identity, cloud, network or application security. You configure controls yourself, not just review them.

- Broad Security Fluency: solid understanding of core security domains and how they interact to defend an enterprise environment.

- Technical Audit Mindset: you can “check the homework” of other teams and know exactly where to look to verify whether a system is truly compliant with CIS Benchmarks or internal standards.

- Detection and Response: proficiency in log analysis and security telemetry, able to troubleshoot an incident across network, endpoint, application and cloud logs to find the smoking gun.

- Scripting: basic to intermediate scripting skills (e.g., PowerShell, Python) to automate administrative tasks and security validations.

- Soft Skills: clear communicator who translates technical risk for different audiences, works controls through other teams and takes ownership of their work.

- Languages: fluent English; German is a plus.

Bonus Skills

- Specialist depth in one or more areas such as cloud security, endpoint and identity (e.g., Microsoft ecosystem), network security (e.g., SASE, segmentation) or application security.

- Relevant certifications (e.g., OSCP, GIAC, CISSP, SC-200, AZ-500) and experience applying frameworks such as CIS Benchmarks, NIST or ISO 27001.

postings.title: Director Production Engineering (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As Director of Production Engineering, you are accountable for the end-to-end production engineering capability across all manufacturing operations. Your mission is to industrialize development outputs into repeatable, scalable, and compliant serial production, ensuring manufacturing readiness, process stability, quality, cost efficiency, and on-time delivery. You lead the team that converts early procedures into robust production standards, embeds them in PLM/MES systems, and drives continuous improvement across the factory.

You act as the primary interface between Engineering (design & development) and Manufacturing (production & operations)—ensuring requirements, procedures, tooling, documentation, test strategies, and digital manufacturing infrastructure are aligned for high-rate, high-quality execution.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

1) Production engineering strategy & leadership

- Define and execute the production engineering roadmap, including industrialization strategy, standardization, and scalability for serial production.

- Lead and develop a team of production/process/manufacturing engineers; set goals, coaching plans, hiring needs, and performance standards.

- Establish clear governance for process ownership, engineering change implementation, and cross-functional decision-making.

2) Assembly, integration & test (AIT) process ownership

- Own manufacturing process definition across:

- Assembly: mechanical/electrical build procedures, torque specs, critical process parameters, work instructions.

- Integration: subsystem integration strategy (e.g., avionics, propulsion, communications), sequencing, interfaces, and acceptance criteria.

- Testing: functional, subsystem, and system-level test strategy; test readiness, execution plans, and troubleshooting methodology.

- Ensure processes are repeatable, auditable, and optimized for safety, throughput, and quality.

3) Industrialization & manufacturing readiness (NPI / transfer to production)

- Coordinate with development teams to receive initial procedures and convert them into production-ready standards (control plans, critical-to-quality characteristics where relevant).

- Drive manufacturing readiness reviews, line readiness, and process qualification for new products, variants, or upgrades.

- Lead the “first builds”/pilot runs, capturing learnings and stabilizing procedures for volume execution.

4) Digital manufacturing (PLM/MES) & configuration control

- Own the production engineering contribution to PLM/MES:

- Translate procedures into structured digital work instructions.

- Ensure traceability, configuration control, and alignment of as-built data.

- Oversee creation and maintenance of:

- mBOM (Manufacturing Bill of Materials)

- BOP (Bill of Process)

- Routings, work centers, and data collection points for quality and traceability.

- Ensure engineering changes are implemented cleanly and quickly, with minimal disruption to production.

5) Documentation, compliance & quality partnership

- Ensure complete, consistent documentation for:

- Work instructions, process specifications, test reports, NCRs (non-conformance reports), deviations/waivers, and as-built configurations.

- Partner with Quality to build robust nonconformance management and corrective action systems (root cause, containment, RCCA & PA).

- Ensure processes meet applicable regulatory, customer, and internal compliance requirements.

6) Cross-functional execution & production support

- Serve as senior escalation point for technical blockers in production: diagnose recurring issues, direct corrective actions, and prevent reoccurrence.

- Align with Supply Chain and Operations on:

- Kitting strategy, material availability, critical path timelines, and constraint removal.

- Coordinate engineering support coverage and readiness for shifts, rate increases, and critical campaigns.

7) Continuous improvement, cost & throughput

- Support Lean Team on Lean/CI initiatives to improve:

- Yield, cycle time, takt adherence, OEE, scrap/rework reduction, and labor efficiency.

- Establish KPIs and operating mechanisms (tier meetings, weekly business reviews) to track and improve production engineering performance.

- Build business cases for capital investments (test equipment, tooling, automation) and manage the budget for your scope.

8) Capability building: training & knowledge management

- Build a strong knowledge-transfer system between engineers and technicians:

- Training plans, certification matrices, standardized visual work instructions, and lessons-learned libraries.

- Ensure procedures are systematically categorized, version-controlled, and easily accessible to production teams.

Success measures (typical KPIs)

- Improved first-pass yield, reduced NCR rate, reduced rework hours

- Reduced cycle time and improved on-time delivery

- Faster and cleaner engineering change implementation

- Increased process stability (fewer repeat issues, fewer line stops)

- Strong audit outcomes and complete traceability / as-built compliance

- High team engagement, retention, and capability maturity

Qualification Checklist

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Aerospace, Automotive, Industrial Engineering, or similar.

- Significant experience in production/manufacturing engineering, industrialization, manufacturing operations—ideally across complex electromechanical systems.

- Proven leadership experience managing teams and cross-functional stakeholders.

- Strong working knowledge of PLM and/or MES, and structured manufacturing artifacts such as mBOM/BOP, routings, work instructions, and configuration control.

- Demonstrated ability in troubleshooting and structured problem solving (e.g., 8D, Ishikawa, 5-Why).

postings.title: Fluids Engineer (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As a Fluids Engineer in the Reusability Program, you analyse propellant behaviour across changing thermal conditions, transient operating states, and mission phases including ascent, shutdown, coast, reentry, and relight. Your work directly drives propellant management, pressurization, and feed system design for next‑generation reusable launch vehicles.

Your Role in Our Space Mission

- Define and analyse the overall propellant management architecture, including propellant location, acquisition strategy, residuals, depletion behaviour, and their interaction across mission phases

- Analyse microgravity and low-acceleration propellant dynamics, including propellant surface behaviour modelled with VOF methods and coupled heat and mass transfer, to drive architectural choices

- Derive tank pressurization concepts from mission requirements and reusability constraints, including transient behaviour across mission phases

- Perform NPSP and inlet margin trades, including the influence of propellant thermal state and transient operating conditions on engine behaviour

- Analyse propellant routing, including feedlines and valves, with focus on transients, operability, and reuse robustness

- Define pressurization and consumables architecture in the context of reusability, including sizing logic, margins, and operational envelopes

- Develop reduced order models from high‑fidelity analyses to support vehicle‑level and program‑level trade studies

Qualification Checklist

Education & Technical Background

- Degree in mechanical, aerospace, or chemical engineering, or a closely related field

- Strong fundamentals in fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, and cryogenic systems

- Solid understanding of multiphase flow, including liquid–vapor interfaces and heat and mass transfer

Experience

- 3–5 years of experience in propulsion, fluids, or propellant management related roles

- Hands‑on experience analysing propellant behaviour at system or architecture level, not only single components

- Practical experience with VOF or comparable multiphase modelling, including thermal effects and free‑surface behaviour

- Exposure to microgravity or low‑acceleration propellant dynamics and their impact on system operability

- Experience deriving or contributing to tank pressurization architectures, including transient behaviour

- Experience abstracting high‑fidelity analysis into reduced order models for vehicle or program‑level trade studies

Skills & Competencies

- Ability to derive propellant management and pressurization architectures from mission requirements, operating envelopes, and reusability constraints

- Capability to quantitatively assess trade‑offs between propellant management concepts using first‑principles analysis, scaling laws, and targeted high‑fidelity simulations

- Critical judgement of model assumptions, numerical limitations, and validity ranges

- Comfortable balancing analysis fidelity, computational cost, and engineering timelines

- Clear communication of complex fluid behaviour to non‑fluids specialists

- Structured, physics‑driven problem‑solving mindset

- Fluent in English (German is a plus)

postings.location: Ottobrunn, Bavaria, Germany; Parsdorf, Bavaria, Germany
postings.description:
Mission Brief

Die Aufgabe besteht hauptsächlich darin, die Fachabteilungen fundiert zur Auswahl geeigneter Komponenten der gesamten Messkette für das Flüssigkeitsraketentriebwerk von Isar Aerospace zu beraten. Sobald der Testbetrieb beginnt, wird der Techniker die Test- und Antriebsingenieure bei der Durchführung ihrer Testkampagnen an Raketentriebwerksprototypen und deren Teilsystemen unterstützen.

Deine Rolle in unserer Space Mission:

- Unterstützung bei der Kalibrierung, Instandhaltung und Wartung unserer Mess- & Prüfmittel

- Selbstständige Installation des Messequipments (Sensorik, Verkabelung, ggf. Messdatenerfassung) für verschiedenste Versuchsaufbauten an unseren Prüfständen, Testeinrichtungen und in unseren Niederlassungen.

- Unterstützung der Kollegen durch die Inbetriebnahme, Überprüfung und Betreuung der vorhandenen Messtechnik-Komponenten (mechanisch, elektrisch und computergestützt)

- Applikation von Dehnungsmesstreifen (DMS) auf Materialproben oder Strukturteilen zur Erfassung der Kennwerte und Aufbereitung dieser Daten, um beratend für Design und Auslegung zu wirken

- Tatkräftige Unterstützung der Projekt- und Testteams während der Durchführung größerer Testkampagnen

- Fundierte Beratung interner Kollegen / Abteilungen zur Auswahl geeigneter Komponenten der gesamten Messkette für unterschiedlichste Bauteil-, Komponenten- und System-Tests speziell im Hinblick auf Vakuum und Niedrig- oder Hochtemperaturbereich

- Inventarisierung sowie Verwaltung elektrischer/elektronischer Messmittel, Überwachung der Kalibrierintervalle und Sicherstellen der Einsatzfähigkeit.

Qualifikationscheckliste

- Staatlich geprüfter Techniker der Fachrichtung Elektrotechnik, Mechatronik oder vergleichbare Qualifikation

- Ein hohes Verantwortungsbewusstsein, ausgeprägte Qualitätsorientierung und eine strukturierte und eigenständige Arbeitsweise

- Eine schnelle Auffassungsgabe zur raschen Einarbeitung in neue Aufgaben und eine ausgeprägte „Hands-on“-Mentalität

- Teamarbeit

- Gültiger Führerschein - Klasse B

- Gutes Englisch, Deutsch verhandlungssicher

- Mietkleidung mit Wäscheservice: Genieße stressfreie Arbeitskleidung mit unserem praktischen Mietkleidungs- und Wäscheservice

- Und vieles mehr! Entdecke zusätzliche Vorteile und Vergünstigungen, wenn du Teil unseres Teams wirst.

Isar Aerospace ist Vorreiter der New Space Industrie mit dem Ziel einen besseren, schnelleren und kostengünstigeren Zugang zum Weltraum zu ermöglichen.

postings.title: Launch Operations Engineer (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As a Launch Operations Engineer, you’ll join the team in Germany that shapes how our missions come to life. From the moment a campaign is conceived, we are aligning global launch sites, synchronizing teams and defining the operational path that ultimately determines how—and whether—the rocket leaves the ground.

Within the global Launch Operations team, you stand at the core of our mission: transforming complex campaigns into repeatable, scalable and reliable operations over multiple launch sites. Your work creates the structure that enables teams across the world to execute with confidence and precision.

When a campaign moves from planning to execution, you step directly into the field—joining local teams on site, supporting coordination efforts in the company, and operations both inside and outside the control room. In these moments, you are a key part of turning months of preparation into a successful launch day.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Support in coordinating and preparing launch and stage acceptance campaigns end‑to‑end, ensuring full launch system readiness.

- Develop a deep understanding of our launch system to support operational decisions, even under pressure. You use this knowledge to guide local teams and maintain global alignment.

- Work directly with the test or launch director to set and improve the operational envelope before the rocket reaches the pad.

- As our launch cadence grows and additional sites come online, you will contribute to our team shaping the future of multi‑site launch operations and define how our global team executes missions.

- Feeding flight experience directly back into engineering teams, ensuring that operational insights continuously improve our system design.

Qualification Checklist

- At least 3-5 years of experience in the space sector or a comparable high‑stakes environment, with a strong background in mission or operational roles, ideally including launch‑related responsibilities

- Degree in aerospace, mechanical, electrical engineering or a comparable engineering discipline

- System-level technical understanding of launch vehicles and their subsystems

- Demonstrated autonomy and a solution-oriented mindset

- Experience in multidisciplinary troubleshooting and cross‑functional coordination

- Ability to maintain clarity and performance in high‑stress, long‑duration operational settings

- Strong organizational discipline, situational awareness, and ability to lead within diverse teams

postings.description:
Mission Brief

We are seeking a hands-on Manager Network & Systems Administration to lead, maintain, and modernize our hybrid infrastructure. In this role, you will act as both a technical lead and an infrastructure owner, bridging our on-premise virtualization, enterprise networking, and multi-cloud environments.

This is a hands-on lead position designed for a senior engineer who excels at architecture, network engineering, and troubleshooting while serving as the primary technical authority for our infrastructure. You will be responsible for end-to-end reliability, system security, network connectivity, and overseeing automated deployment workflows—from bare-metal hypervisors to cloud routing.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

Technical Leadership & Operations

- Hands-on Infrastructure Leadership: Serve as the primary technical subject matter expert (SME) and escalation point for all systems, virtualization, and network architecture.

- Vendor & Asset Management: Oversee infrastructure vendor relationships, license agreements, hardware lifecycles, and service level agreements (SLAs).

- Incident & Capacity Planning: Lead major incident responses, perform root-cause analysis (RCA), and proactively monitor capacity across storage, compute, and network links.

Multi-Cloud & Virtualization Management

- Hybrid & Multi-Cloud Administration: Design, secure, and maintain scalable infrastructure across Azure, AWS, and IONOS Cloud.

- On-Premise Virtualization: Oversee, optimize, and maintain our enterprise hypervisor clusters using VMware vSphere (ESXi/vCenter) and Proxmox VE (KVM/LXC).

- Disaster Recovery & Data Protection: Plan, implement, and test automated backup, recovery, and high-availability strategies across all platforms.

- Infrastructure Automation Concepts: Understand and support Infrastructure as Code (IaC) workflows (Terraform/Ansible) to streamline server provisioning, configuration management, and patching.

Enterprise Networking & Security

- Network & Connectivity Management: Design, configure, and troubleshoot complex network architecture involving Cloud VPCs, Site-to-Site IPsec VPNs, VLAN segmentation, DNS, DHCP, and firewalls.

- Traffic Management: Manage load balancing, ingress routing, and perimeter security to ensure high availability and zero-trust access principles.

- Cloud Platforms: Proven experience managing production environments in Azure and AWS (familiarity with IONOS Cloud is a major plus).

- Networking & Firewalls: Strong understanding of TCP/IP, BGP/OSPF routing, DNS, Load Balancing (HAProxy/Nginx), enterprise Firewalls, and IPsec VPNs.

- 5+ years of hands-on experience in Systems Administration, Network Engineering, or Cloud Architecture, with demonstrated experience acting in a lead or senior capacity.

- Proven track record of architecting, deploying, and maintaining hybrid cloud and multi-site network environments.

- Strong communication skills with the ability to bridge technical requirements and business objectives.

postings.description:
Mission Brief

As the Managing Director Launch Site Canada, you will be the first person on the ground and the driving force behind establishing our Canadian launch site and operations. This is a rare opportunity to shape a national spaceport presence from day one. In the early years, your primary mission will be to build the foundation for future launch campaigns: securing regulatory approvals, developing infrastructure, establishing operational processes, and assembling a high performing team. You will lead the development of the site, prepare all systems and procedures for launch readiness, and ensure the Canadian entity is fully compliant, well governed, and aligned with our global organization. Once the site becomes operational, you will oversee launch campaigns, pad operations, and mission execution.

You will report to the Canadian Board of Directors and disciplinarily to the VP Mission & Launch Operations and work closely with global teams in Germany, Norway and Sweden across Launch Operations, Engineering, HR, Finance, Legal, and Infrastructure.

postings.description:

We deliver the half of the rocket that stays on the ground. As Senior Mechanical Ground Systems Engineer at the Ground Systems department of Isar Aerospace, you will take part in shaping the development of the Ground Systems infrastructure. This includes ground equipment such as the Launch Table, Transporter/Erector, and Hold-Down-Release Mechanism as fundamental parts of the Launchpad, but also the design of equipment for Testing Facilities, R&D, qualification and acceptance of propulsion systems and rocket stages. You will work in close cooperation with other engineering departments as well, such as Propulsion Technology and Launch Vehicle, since their requirements drive the design of the ground support equipment.

- Taking responsibility, ownership and accountability for mechanical (sub)systems as part of larger projects

- Managing requirements proactively between stakeholders for own (sub)systems as part of larger projects and defining Engineering Change Requests

postings.title: Mitarbeiter interne Logistik (m/w/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

Als Teil des internen Logistikteams ist es Deine Hauptaufgabe, dafür zu sorgen, dass die täglichen Abläufe und Prozesse rund um die interne Logistik in der Produktion reibungslos und effizient funktionieren.

Deine Rolle in unserer Space Mission:

- Allgemeine Lagertätigkeiten ausführen: Be- und Entladen von Waren, Buchen des Wareneingangs, Kommissionieren, Ein- und Auslagern von Waren, Umlagerungen zwischen verschiedenen Lagern und an die verschiedenen Produktionsschritte

- Die Rückverfolgbarkeit der Waren im Lager sicherstellen (korrekte Kennzeichnung, Lagerung, etc.)

- Abstimmung mit verschiedenen Abteilungen, die an der internen Logistik beteiligt sind z.B. Einkauf und Produktion, und die Lagerprozesse an den Produktionsbedarf anpassen

- Optimierungen im Hinblick auf Ressourcen, Prozesse und Dienstleistungen vorantreiben, um den höchstmöglichen Gewinn zu erzielen

- Dokumentation von sämtliche Warenbewegungen im Lager

- Die Unversehrtheit und korrekte Lagerung der Waren im Lager sicherstellen (gemäß den Anforderungen an Temperatur, Luftfeuchtigkeit, Gewicht, Gefahrstoffe...)

- Durchführung von regelmäßigen Inventuren

- Nach Wareneingang und Einlagerung den Zuschnitt von Rohmaterialien durchführen

- Den Lagerbereich sauber und ordentlich halten

- Mit Flurförderfahrzeugen (z. B. Gabelstapler) Waren im Lager bewegen

- Abgeschlossene Ausbildung als Logistiker oder Quereinstieg mit IHK-Weiterbildung möglich

- 3 -5 Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Logistik, Lagerverwaltung oder in ähnlichen Bereichen

- Relevante Erfahrung im Umgang mit Lagerverwaltungssystemen

- Staplerschein

- Fließende Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse

- Führerschein bis 3,5 t

- Teamfähigkeit

- Belastbarkeit

- Bereitschaft zum Schichtdienst

Bonusfähigkeiten

- Kenntnisse in Ladungssicherung

- Erfahrung mit SAP

- Reisebereitschaft

- 30 Tage Urlaub: Genieße die freien Tage, um dich zu entspannen und neue Energie zu tanken

- Betriebliche Altersvorsorge: Sichere deine Zukunft mit unserer betrieblichen Altersvorsorge, bei der der Arbeitgeber nach der Probezeit 20% bezuschusst

- Subventioniertes Mittagessen: Bleibe jeden Tag mit köstlichen, subventionierten Mittagessen energiegeladen

- Mietkleidung mit Wäscheservice: Genieße stressfreie Arbeitskleidung mit unserem praktischen Mietkleidungs- und Wäscheservice

Isar Aerospace ist Vorreiter der New Space Industrie mit dem Ziel einen besseren, schnelleren und kostengünstigeren Zugang zum Weltraum zu ermöglichen.

Unsere Mission ist es, zur Demokratisierung des Weltraums beizutragen, um das Leben auf der Erde heute und für zukünftige Generationen zu verbessern.

postings.title: Principal System Architect, Spectrum (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As Principal System Architect for Reusability, you will lead exploration of the reusable-launcher design space and drive convergence towards a coherent vehicle architecture. Using models and analyses developed by specialist teams, you will identify the most valuable design paths, direct further investigation and make architecture decisions that balance performance, development risk, operability, lifecycle cost and profitability.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Own the end-to-end architecture of the reusable launch vehicle, including its configuration, interfaces, operational concept and key dependencies.

- Define the architecture exploration strategy: structure the design space, select promising paths and determine where further analysis or testing is required.

- Lead multidisciplinary trades using inputs and model outputs from specialist teams; challenge assumptions, expose dependencies and resolve conflicting objectives.

- Drive architecture decisions and convergence, maintaining clear rationale, configuration baselines and priorities for the next exploration cycle.

- Balance vehicle performance and recovery with production, supply chain, logistics, launch operations, refurbishment, cadence, lifecycle cost, market demand and profitability.

- Align engineering, operations, program, finance and commercial stakeholders around the selected architecture and communicate decisions, risks and remaining trades clearly.

Qualification Checklist

- Extensive launch-vehicle architecture experience, including direct work on rocket development programs.

- Demonstrated experience with reusable launch vehicles, recovery architectures or reuse-driven vehicle design.

- Proven ownership of multidisciplinary architecture trades and high-impact design decisions.

- Deep understanding of reusable-launcher architectures, subsystem interactions and the dependencies connecting vehicle design, recovery and operations.

- Strong multidisciplinary knowledge across propulsion, fluids, structures, avionics, trajectory, production, logistics, launch operations and refurbishment.

- Ability to interpret integrated model outputs, judge their assumptions and limitations, and translate them into architecture decisions and targeted follow-on work.

- Sound systems-engineering and configuration-management knowledge, with strong judgement in lifecycle cost, operational economics and profitability trades.

- Decisive cross-functional leader who can challenge local optima, set direction under uncertainty and create alignment without relying on line authority.

- Clear strategic communicator across engineering, program and executive audiences.

postings.description:

As a Product Assurance Engineer, Launch Operations, you will join our team on the beautiful arctic island of Andøya to perform test and launch campaigns of our Spectrum launch vehicle. You will act as a control instance for the quality and compliance of ground equipment, processes, and procedures, while also closely working with our Quality department based in Germany to ensure the quality of the flight hardware.

To do so, you will carry out in-process and final inspections, document reviews, and follow-up non-conformance reports. You will be following established processes, but will also have the opportunity to introduce new frameworks tailored to this launch site.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Be involved in and follow-up on acceptance testing of flight hardware

- Review processes and procedures, and enforce the applicable document management

- Follow-up on non-conformance reports and risks, including the mitigating actions

- Set-up and maintain calibration plans for tools, equipment and systems

- Ensure proper and continuous documentation

Qualification Checklist

- Relevant engineering qualification or engineering bachelor’s or master’s degree

- Experience in quality inspections and assurance involving hardware (preferably including assemblies)

- Experience with document management

- Experience with non-conformity processes and root cause analysis

- Ability to perform in high-stress environments

- Highly organised, effective team player with high attention to detail

- Able to adjust self-sufficiently and quickly to a highly dynamic work environment

postings.description:
Mission Brief

Die Rolle des Production Mechanic CNC im Bereich Pre & Post Processing übernimmt technische Aufgaben bei der Vorbereitung sowie der Nachbearbeitung von Bauteilen und stellt durch fachliche Kompetenz die Qualität und Prozesssicherheit der Produktionsaufträge im Tagesgeschäft sicher.

Deine Rolle in unserer Space Mission:

Fachliche Aufgaben:

- Entgraten, Schleifen und Polieren von Bauteilen gemäß Qualitäts- und Zeichnungsvorgaben

- Markieren, Labeln und Kennzeichnen von Bauteilen nach technischer Dokumentation

- Reinigung und finale Oberflächenvorbereitung

- Fachgerechte Installation von Gewindeeinsätzen (z. B. Helicoils)

- Durchführung verschiedener Einpress- und Fügeprozesse inkl. Vorbereitung der benötigten Komponenten

- Zusägen von Rohmaterial

- Abarbeiten und Rückmelden von Fertigungsaufträgen im MES-System

- Dokumentation der bearbeiteten Aufträge und relevanter Prozessdaten

- Mitarbeit bei der Optimierung von Prozessen, Abläufen und Standards im Bereich Nachbearbeitung

- Erkennen und Melden fehlender Materialien, Werkzeuge oder Hilfsmittel

Qualifikationscheckliste

- Abgeschlossene Ausbildung als Feinwerkmechaniker, Werkzeugbauer, Industriemechaniker, Zerspanungsmechaniker und ähnliche wünschenswert.

- Gerne auch Quereinsteiger wie z.B. Goldschmied und Zahntechniker

- Erfahrung in den Bereichen Entgraten, Schleifen, Polieren

- Manuelle Nachbearbeitung empfindlicher Bauteile

- Verständnis von Passungen und Oberflächenqualitäten

- Erfahrung mit Füge- und Montagearbeiten (mechanisch)

- Gute Deutschkenntnisse erforderlich; Englischkenntnisse wünschenswert

Bonusfähigkeiten

- Sehr stark ausgeprägtes Qualitätsbewusstsein

- Sehr sorgfältige, gewissenhafte Arbeitsweise

- Ruhige, saubere Arbeitsweise bei manueller Nachbearbeitung

- Offenheit für neue Technologien (Automation, Messmittel, Software)

- Sauberes und klares Dokumentieren von Prüfungen, Abweichungen und Bearbeitungsschritten

- Selbstständiges Planen der eigenen Arbeitsschritte

- Eigenverantwortliches Handeln im Rahmen der Produktionsrichtlinie

Benefits:

- Mitarbeiterbeteiligungsprogramm: Wir möchten dich an unserem Erfolg beteiligen durch unsere virtuellen Unternehmensaktien.

- 30 Tage Urlaub: Genieße die freien Tage, um dich zu entspannen und neue Energie zu tanken

- Betriebliche Altersvorsorge: Sichere deine Zukunft mit unserer betrieblichen Altersvorsorge, bei der der Arbeitgeber nach der Probezeit 20% bezuschusst

- Subventioniertes Mittagessen: Bleibe jeden Tag mit köstlichen, subventionierten Mittagessen energiegeladen

- ÖPNV-Ticket: Pendle stressfrei mit einem vollständig finanzierten Deutschlandticket

- Mietkleidung mit Wäscheservice: Genieße stressfreie Arbeitskleidung mit unserem praktischen Mietkleidungs- und Wäscheservice

- Und vieles mehr! Entdecke zusätzliche Vorteile und Vergünstigungen, wenn du Teil unseres Teams wirst.

Isar Aerospace ist Vorreiter der New Space Industrie mit dem Ziel einen besseren, schnelleren und kostengünstigeren Zugang zum Weltraum zu ermöglichen.

Unsere Mission ist es, zur Demokratisierung des Weltraums beizutragen, um das Leben auf der Erde heute und für zukünftige Generationen zu verbessern.

postings.title: Propulsion Design Engineer, Propulsion - Engine Integration (w/m/f)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As a Propulsion Design Engineer, you will drive the development of engine hardware from initial concept through qualification and production. You will be responsible for the design, analysis, and integration of engine structural components, piping, and subsystem packaging, with a strong focus on component placement, mass optimisation, and manufacturability. This includes defining engine architecture, optimising routing and interfaces, and developing design solutions that reduce weight, part count, and costs, while ensuring performance and reliability. The role requires close collaboration with multidisciplinary engineering teams and a strong understanding of engine architecture and system-level integration.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Own complex engine assemblies from concept to hardware delivery, balancing technical scope, schedule, and integration requirements.

- Design and develop engine hardware and fluid routing using CAD tools, including detailed 3D models and manufacturing drawings.

- Drive the iterative development and continuous optimisation of flight-proven hardware.

- Implement engine layout improvements while complying with engine functional requirements.

- Define and manage interfaces with adjacent systems and collaborate closely with fluid system, combustion, structures, manufacturing, and testing teams.

- Perform structural and thermal analyses to ensure component performance and system reliability.

Qualification Checklist

- M.Sc. or M.Eng. in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.

- Proven engineering excellence and experience solving complex technical problems.

postings.title: Quality & Test Technician (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As a Quality & Test Technician (Electronics Manufacturing), you are responsible for ensuring the quality, functionality, and readiness of electronic assemblies throughout the production process. You will inspect printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs), perform electrical testing, operate advanced manufacturing equipment, verify conformal coating quality, and support final assembly and product release activities.

This role is critical to maintaining product quality, manufacturing reliability, and customer satisfaction. You will work closely with Production, Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, and Test Engineering teams to ensure products meet all workmanship, functional, and traceability requirements before release.

postings.title: Recovery Operations Engineer (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As a Recovery Operations Engineer in the Reusability Program, you define and mature the CONOPS for post‑flight recovery, refurbishment, and return‑to‑flight of reusable launch vehicle elements. You enable safe, repeatable, and cost‑efficient reuse by embedding recovery and refurbishment considerations into vehicle design, ground operations, and long‑term fleet operability from the outset.

Your Role in Our Space Mission

- Define and evolve recovery Concept of Operations (CONOPS), covering primary recovery scenarios as well as fallback scenarios, from landing through return‑to‑flight

- Evaluate and down‑select launch sites, landing zones, and ranges with respect to recovery feasibility, safety, and operations

- Specify and assess recovery ground support equipment (GSE), including cranes, transport frames, barges, and port infrastructure

- Define refurbishment and recycle processes, including inspection flows, repair scope, turnaround timelines, and reuse limits

- Drive maintainability and operability requirements into vehicle and system design

- Support integration and payload processing concepts where recovery impacts launch‑site operations

- Contribute to fleet and lifecycle management strategies, including inspection intervals and retirement criteria

- Develop and maintain operational cost models, including recovery, refurbishment, infrastructure, and reuse cost functions, and support cost estimation and trade studies to inform architectural and program‑level decisions

Qualification Checklist

Education & Technical Background

- Engineering education in aerospace, mechanical, civil, naval, industrial, or a closely related field, or equivalent senior industry experience

- Technical background in launcher ground operations plus recovery and refurbishment concepts for reusable launch vehicle hardware

- Proven knowledge of transport, handling, lifting, storage, inspection, and repair of large aerospace hardware and associated ground support equipment

- Proven knowledge of large‑scale logistics and ground infrastructure as primary drivers of operability, cost, and turnaround time in a reusable launch vehicle fleet

Experience

- 5–10+ years in launch vehicle programs, recovery programs, or large‑scale aerospace hardware projects

- Direct involvement in designing and evaluating end‑to‑end CONOPS, covering recovery logistics, ground support equipment, refurbishment, maintainability, and return‑to‑flight

- Practical work with large ground support equipment and infrastructure, including recovery assets, lifting systems, transport solutions, hazardous substances supply systems and launch-site or port environments

- Hands-on exposure to launch vehicle or aircraft refurbishment and post‑operation processing, including inspection strategies, repair scope definition, structural and systems assessments, and reuse or return‑to‑service considerations.

- Demonstrated ability to assess how recovery and ground operations concepts drive launcher architecture, interfaces, access requirements, and design margins

- Proven involvement in operational trade studies, addressing feasibility, cost drivers, turnaround time, and risk across alternative recovery and refurbishment approaches

Skills & Competencies

- Ability to architect recovery and refurbishment CONOPS that are technically executable and scale with fleet growth

- Strong judgement balancing launcher design, ground support equipment capability, logistics constraints, safety, cost, and schedule

- Deep practical knowledge of ground support equipment-driven constraints and their impact on recovery methods and launcher interfaces

- Clear command of maintainability and refurbishment drivers, including access, wear mechanisms, handling damage, and inspection effort

- Structured decision‑making under uncertainty, grounded in experience with real hardware, infrastructure, and field operations

postings.title: Senior Engine Cycle Engineer (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

You will own the engine cycle and the top level technical architecture of a pump fed liquid rocket engine. As the responsible engineer you translate mission and vehicle needs into an integrated engine design, establish the key performance trades, and make sure every major sub system converges on one coherent, testable and manufacturable solution.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Build, maintain and validate engine cycle models across nominal, throttled and off nominal operating conditions, including start up and shutdown transients.

- Lead cycle trade studies and sensitivity analyses to optimise performance and identify design drivers, constraints and technical risks.

- Perform top level engine sizing and define the principal operating points and component interface conditions.

- Drive architecture and design trade offs across combustion devices, turbomachinery, valves, feed systems, ignition, controls, structures, thermal management and engine layout.

- Own the top level engine requirements, assumptions, interface definitions and technical budgets.

- Act as the technical decision driver for cross functional design issues, and keep decisions documented, traceable and backed by analysis and test evidence.

- Own the technical development roadmap and timeline: guide design iterations, prioritise maturation activities, and define the analyses, breadboards and tests that retire the highest risks.

- Coordinate technical reviews and give clear recommendations to Propulsion leadership and to the programme and vehicle teams.

Qualification Checklist

- MSc in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering or a comparable technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

- Several years in liquid rocket engine development, with real responsibility for engine cycle analysis, engine architecture or propulsion system integration.

- Hands on experience with high pressure, pump fed liquid rocket engine cycles: designing, analysing, developing or testing them.

- Excellent understanding of engine cycles, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics and turbomachinery power balance.

- Steady state cycle modelling, top level engine sizing and performance prediction.

- Experience planning and coordinating multidisciplinary engine development or test campaigns, and driving a technical roadmap to agreed timelines.

- Proficiency in Python, MATLAB or a comparable programming language.

- Strong technical ownership and systems thinking, and the confidence to decide with incomplete information.

- Fluent in English.

- Willingness to travel occasionally for test and launch operations.

Bonus Skills

- Experience with transient cycle modelling: start up, shutdown, throttling and off nominal conditions.

- Experience taking an engine design from cycle definition and system level trades into hardware and test.

- Experience analysing engine control, operability, stability or failure cases.

- Enough breadth across valves, feed systems, ignition, controls, structures and thermal management to arbitrate trade offs between those disciplines.

- Experience correlating models against hot fire test data.

postings.title: Senior Launch Operations Engineer (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As a Senior Launch Operations Engineer, you’ll join the team in Germany that shapes how our missions come to life. From the moment a campaign is conceived, you are the one aligning global launch sites, synchronizing teams and defining the operational path that ultimately determines how—and whether—the rocket leaves the ground.

Within the global Launch Operations team, you stand at the core of our mission: transforming complex campaigns into repeatable, scalable and reliable operations over multiple launch sites. Your work creates the structure that enables teams across the world to execute with confidence and precision.

When a campaign moves from planning to execution, you step directly into the field—joining local teams on site, leading coordination efforts in the company, and operations both inside and outside the control room. In these moments, you carry the responsibility of turning months of preparation into a successful launch day.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Coordinate and prepare launch and stage acceptance campaigns end‑to‑end, ensuring full launch system readiness. Over time, you can grow into a test or launch director role for dedicated missions.

- Develop a deep understanding of our launch system to make sound operational decisions, even under pressure. You use this knowledge to guide local teams and maintain global alignment.

- Own mission‑level configuration management, keeping design, manufacturing, assembly and testing tightly aligned with mission goals. Your decisions set the operational envelope long before the rocket reaches the pad.

- As our launch cadence grows and additional sites come online, you will contribute to our team shaping the future of multi‑site launch operations and define how our global team executes missions.

- Feeding flight experience directly back into engineering teams, ensuring that operational insights continuously improve our system design.

Qualification Checklist

- At least five years of experience in the space sector or a comparable high‑stakes environment, with a strong background in mission or operational roles, ideally including launch‑related responsibilities

- Degree in aerospace, mechanical, electrical engineering or a comparable engineering discipline

- System-level technical understanding of launch vehicles and their subsystems

- Demonstrated autonomy and a solution-oriented mindset

- Experience in multidisciplinary troubleshooting and cross‑functional coordination

- Ability to maintain clarity and performance in high‑stress, long‑duration operational settings

- Strong organizational discipline, situational awareness, and ability to lead within diverse teams

postings.title: Senior Security Engineer (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

You are the guardian and the challenger of our security posture. At Isar Aerospace, the systems that build our rockets and the ground systems that launch them are mission critical, and protecting them takes more than good design. It takes someone who will attack their own work to be sure it holds.

We are looking for a deeply hands-on Senior Security Engineer. You live in the consoles, the rule sets and the code. You own our secure access and network security controls, our endpoint and identity security stack, and our detection content, and you operate them yourself rather than directing from the sidelines. You wear two hats: the Builder who implements and runs the controls that keep us safe, and the Adversary who keeps testing whether those controls and detections actually fire.

This is a senior engineering role with the spirit of an architect. You are expected to design what you operate, not just configure it: pick the pattern, write it down, and make it hold at fleet scale. A versatile engineer with real depth, comfortable switching from a firewall rule set to a detection query to a directory hardening sprint in the same week, and a technical anchor others lean on.

Your Role in Our Space Mission

SASE and Network Security

- Own and operate our SASE platform, including revamping Internet Security policies and redefining Private Access policies.

- Drive firewall security with the network team: own network security engineering and segmentation strategy, analyze rule sets, identify gaps, and see remediation through together with network engineering, who own the devices.

- Coordinate firewall-adjacent controls: IPS, AV, sandboxing and DDoS protection.

- Manage our DNS security and WAF solutions, including our edge and CDN-based protection services.

Security Posture and Hardening

- Apply CIS Benchmarks to raise posture across firewalls, endpoints, our cloud identity platform and our cloud productivity suite.

- Lead the clean-up and hardening of our on-premises and cloud identity directories together with the infrastructure team, then keep both hardened on an ongoing basis.

- Drive our phishing-resistant MFA and privileged access programme, including just-in-time elevation and the remediation of the attack paths we find.

- Own certificate lifecycle and PKI operations: key ceremonies, automated renewal, and input to our post-quantum migration plan.

Detection and Visibility

- Manage and tune our IPS/IDS platforms; write and maintain custom IDS signatures, and operate network sensors for NTA appliances.

- Build and maintain detections in our SIEM and apply MITRE ATT&CK to detection engineering and use-case design in support of the SOC.

- Extend visibility into OT with purpose-built OT monitoring tooling.

- Act as an L3 incident responder for escalated security events, and turn every finding into a fix, a new detection or a hardened configuration.

Security Stack and Automation

- Own our endpoint detection and response, data protection and CASB platforms as their technical owner.

- Script and build internal tooling in PowerShell and Python, so controls and checks run themselves.

Design and Engineering Partnership

- Design what you operate: run threat modeling and attack-path analysis on the systems you own, choose the pattern, and document standards others can execute against.

postings.title: Senior Structures Analysis Engineer, Launch Vehicle Structure (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

You will be responsible for the structural analysis of entire assemblies belonging to our rocket’s primary and secondary structures. From trading design concepts to sizing and validating design iterations and examining the impact of manufacturing deviations, you will play an important role in guiding design decisions and pushing performance and reliability of our structures forward.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Identify failure scenarios and collaborate with design engineers to review and optimize structural designs.

- Define applicable load cases, addressing the impact of thermal, quasi-static loads (arising from random vibrations) etc.

- Analise and provide possible solutions to manufacturing non-conformities

- Develop test plans and support physical testing of components to verify sizing assumptions and qualify hardware.

- Prepare comprehensive stress analysis reports and documentation for internal/external use

- Improve our standards and toolchain for structural verification

- Be familiar with classical design standards and have experience in the use of CAD software

- Provide technical mentorship and guidance to junior engineers within the team

Qualification Checklist

- Degree in the field of Engineering, Aerospace, Mechanical or (Computational) Mechanics, or any other related field.

- At least 8 years of experience in analysing aerospace structures

- Profound knowledge in classical hand-calculations and advanced FE Modelling of aerospace structures (Hypermesh, Optistruct etc)

- Self-motivated, collaborative, and capable of working independently with minimal supervision.

- High degree of independence and confidence in assessing and trading design risks

- Strong engineering intuition with regards to load paths and failure mechanisms

- Holistic perspective on development of structures

- Fluent English

Bonus Skills

- Practical experience in the space sector (preferably in launch vehicle development program).

- Previous experience using CAD, preferably with Siemens NX.

- German language skills

postings.title: Structural Design Engineer, Spectrum (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

As a Structural Design Engineer in the Reusability Department, you will shape the structural architecture of next-generation reusable launch vehicles. Your work will bridge vehicle design, structural analysis, and integrated system layout to enable fast, informed architecture trade studies and development decisions.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Define and evaluate vehicle-level structural loads, load paths, and critical sizing cases across ascent, recovery, landing, and ground operations.

- Develop structural concepts and perform sizing activities using first-principles methods, reduced-order models, and targeted finite element analyses.

- Translate reusable launcher architecture concepts into realistic, rapidly adaptable CAD layouts that support architecture trade studies and vehicle development.

- Assess the integration of primary structures with tanks, fluid systems, aerodynamic surfaces, landing systems, mechanisms, and other vehicle subsystems.

- Create and maintain structural models of appropriate fidelity to evaluate feasibility, mass, stiffness, interfaces, and overall vehicle performance.

- Identify structural drivers, design constraints, and cross-system dependencies to guide architecture decisions and system optimization.

- Support multidisciplinary vehicle development by balancing structural performance, operability, manufacturability, and reuse requirements.

- Communicate structural implications, trade-offs, and recommendations to engineering stakeholders across the program.

Qualification Checklist

- 3-7 years of experience in aerospace, launch vehicles, aircraft structures, or other highly engineered structural products.

- Experience developing structural concepts and layouts from requirements through preliminary design.

- Experience contributing to vehicle-level architecture trades and multidisciplinary system development.

- Strong understanding of structural mechanics, load paths, structural sizing, and vehicle-level structural behavior.

- Proficiency with FEM tools (e.g. Abaqus, Nastran, Ansys, HyperWorks) for both conceptual assessments and targeted detailed analyses.

- Ability to develop reduced-order models and engineering approximations from higher-fidelity analyses.

- Strong CAD skills (e.g. CATIA, Siemens NX or comparable) with the ability to rapidly create and iterate structurally credible vehicle layouts.

- Systems-thinking mindset with the ability to balance structural performance, integration, operability, and program objectives.

- Structured problem solver with sound engineering judgment and a pragmatic approach to trade-offs.

- Fluent in English, both written and spoken.

- Experience with reusable launch vehicles, recovery systems, landing systems, or deployable mechanisms.

- Self-motivated, collaborative, and capable of working independently with moderate guidance.

postings.title: Struktur Fertigungstechniker (m/w/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

In unserem Launcher AIT (Assembly, Integration, Testing) Team bist Du mitverantwortlich für die technisch einwandfreie und pünktliche Auslieferung unserer Launch Vehicles, von der Montage der ersten Strukturelemente über unsere Fluid- & Avionic Systeme bis hin zu Abnahmetests. Unser schlagkräftiges multinationales Team baut und betreut die Flughardware in enger Zusammenarbeit mit unseren Entwicklern sowie dem Integrated Testing Team auf unserer Launch Base.

- Fundierte Kenntnisse in der Be- & Verarbeitung von CFK; Erfahrung in Metallbearbeitung von Vorteil

postings.title: Supplier Quality Engineer (m/f/d)
postings.description:
Mission Brief

The Supplier Quality Engineer is responsible for ensuring externally supplied materials, components, assemblies, and special processes consistently meet company, customer, and regulatory requirements. Reporting within the Quality organization, this role serves as the primary quality interface between the company and its supply base to ensure supplier performance supports safe, reliable, and compliant aerospace manufacturing.
The position leads supplier qualification, supplier performance management, supplier audits, source inspections, and supplier corrective action activities. Working closely with Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Engineering, Product Assurance, and Quality teams, the Supplier Quality Engineer drives continuous improvement throughout the supplier network while reducing supplier-related quality risks.

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

- Plan and execute supplier qualification and approval activities for new and existing suppliers.

- Lead source inspections and verification activities at supplier facilities when required.

- Develop, maintain, and review supplier scorecards and supplier performance metrics.

- Manage supplier nonconformances and supplier corrective action processes to ensure timely and effective resolution.

- Conduct root cause analysis reviews and verify effectiveness of supplier corrective actions.

- Partner with Supply Chain and Engineering teams in supplier selection, development, and risk assessments.

- Support First Article Inspection, qualification, and industrialization activities involving external suppliers.

- Monitor supplier quality trends and proactively identify risks to quality, delivery, and operational performance.

- Drive supplier continuous improvement initiatives focused on defect prevention and process capability enhancement.

- Support incoming inspection organizations with supplier-related quality investigations and containment actions.

- Maintain supplier quality records, audit reports, and compliance documentation in accordance with applicable quality management system requirements.

Qualification Checklist

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or a related technical discipline.

- Experience in Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Product Assurance, or Quality Engineering environments.

- Strong understanding of supplier qualification, supplier development, and supplier performance management processes.

- Experience planning and conducting supplier audits and process assessments.

- Knowledge of root cause analysis methodologies and corrective action systems.

- Understanding of aerospace quality requirements including configuration control, traceability, and product conformity principles.

postings.description:

You will join the Combustion Devices team and take responsibility for the thrust chamber assembly (TCA): injector head, combustion chamber and nozzle. You will design and analyse these components, plan and evaluate the tests that prove them, and work with production to make sure what you design can actually be built, quickly and at scale. Your Role in Our Space Mission:
